question: What is the difference (approx.) between compound interest on Rs. 6000 for 2 years at 20% per annum compounded yearly and half yearly?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest rate for **20% yearly** for 2 years = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100 = **44%**.

Effective interest rate for **10% half-yearly** for 4 periods = **46.41%**.

Difference in effective rate = 46.41% − 44% = **2.41%**.

Difference in amount = 2.41% of ₹6000 = (2.41 ÷ 100) × 6000 = 144.6 ≈ **₹145**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹6000, Rate (R) = 20% p.a., Time (n) = 2 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b61dcd6a11747442537bab5bc4aac67e6743fdc963f79802c175fdda0cc3e705.png] 

**Case 1: Yearly Compounding**

⇒ Amount (A₁) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

⇒ A₁ = 6000(1 + 20/100)² = 6000(1.2)²

⇒ A₁ = 6000 × 1.44 = ₹8640

⇒ CI₁ = 8640 − 6000 = **₹2640**

**Case 2: Half-yearly Compounding**

⇒ New Rate (R') = 20/2 = 10% per half-year

⇒ New Time (n') = 2 × 2 = 4 half-years

⇒ Amount (A₂) = 6000(1 + 10/100)⁴ = 6000(1.1)⁴

⇒ A₂ = 6000 × 1.4641 = ₹8784.6

⇒ CI₂ = 8784.6 − 6000 = **₹2784.6**

**Difference Calculation:**

⇒ Difference = CI₂ − CI₁ = 2784.6 − 2640 = ₹144.6

⇒ Difference ≈ ₹145

**∴ The correct answer is ₹145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

For compounding **k** times a year: A = P(1 + R/(100 × k))ⁿ×k. For half-yearly, k = 2.

Effective Rate of Interest

It is the actual annual interest rate when compounding occurs more than once a year: Rₑff = [(1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1] × 100.

CI and SI Difference (2 years)

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by P(R/100)².
